conviction_note: The findings net to about zero: the Q3 consensus needs a Q2 that included Q1 catch-up to repeat, and Honeywell's aftermarket is parts-constrained, against a ~9.4-day-to-cover short, AAR's +31% repair growth and the new Honeywell distribution rights. abs_move_pct is 8%, rebuilt from confirmed releases (sealed history mixed in AGM/contract 6-Ks). p_up 48, not 50, only because this name sold its last two beats and punished the March print.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $52.7M (Benzinga consensus, updated 2026-10-13, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TATT/earnings-forecasts, via search snippet) to $54.33M (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/TATT, via snippet); EPS $0.43 (Benzinga) vs $0.38 (Earnings Whispers), basis disputed (GAAP vs company-adjusted), so EPS-based findings are capped small. No company guidance exists: management only said 'meaningful full-year revenue and EBITDA growth' and 'excellent revenue visibility for the remainder of 2026' (https://quartr.com/events/tat-technologies-ltd-tatt-q2-2026_F3nhMtcP). Q3 2025 actual was $46.2M, so the bar implies +14-18% YoY.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest 1,256,416 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement (1,333,220 at 09-30, peak 1,496,347 at 09-15; under 400k as recently as May). That is 9.4 days to cover on 133k average volume, per https://equibles.com/stocks/tatt/shortinterest. It is 9.7% of 12.98M shares outstanding. Israeli institutions file 13Gs for roughly half the shares (Meitav 19.48%, Phoenix 8.8%, Migdal 7.3%, Kranot 6.25%, IBI 4.8%, More 4.8%), so the short is roughly 20% of the remaining float. There is no listed option market (baseline: no_options_market), so there is no skew and no implied move. The tape: spot $32.0, 1.5% above the 52-week low, -47.6% from the 52-week high of $61.11 (2026-03-17), -9.1% over 20 days. Sell-side targets are all far above: B. Riley cut $65 to $60 on 2026-10-28, StoneX $66, Lake Street $61, Stifel $53, all Buy.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue consensus of about $52.7-54.3M needs Q2's $52.9M to repeat, but Q2 included Q1 catch-up. The MRO aviation components segment (APU/landing gear, Piedmont) did $27.7M in Q2 (+38.5% YoY) after only about $16.9M in Q1, which was down YoY on supply-chain timing. H1 revenue grew only 10.4% (avg $47.0M/quarter), and Q3 2025 x 1.104 = $51.0M, about 3-6% below the bar. Backlog rose to about $615M from $580M and management claimed 'excellent revenue visibility', which supports Q3 holding near Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from confirmed release dates and Yahoo closes. Q2 2026 (2026-08-05 bmo) revenue $52.9M vs about $44.9M consensus, a +18% beat: +2.3% on the day, then -6.4% the next. Q1 2026 (2026-05-20 bmo) revenue $41.1M vs $40.2M, a small beat from a $32.7 low: +21.0%. Q4 2025 (2026-03-18) on supply-chain and FX worries: -7.5% on the day and -16.3% the next. Q3 2025 (2025-11-12 amc): about +6% after hours, -0.7% close to close. Q2 2025 (2025-08-12): -12.4%. Revenue disappointments are punished, beats are sold or faded.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus moved up to the Q2 run-rate after the 18% beat (from about $44.9M for Q2 to $52.7-54.3M for Q3) without separating out the Q1-to-Q2 catch-up. If the market had priced a sub-bar quarter, estimates would sit near $50-51M, not at Q2's level. The stock's 25% slide since 08-05 may partly reflect this doubt, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: The segment split is in the same 6-K as the Q2 release; the bar comes from separate aggregators (Benzinga, Earnings Whispers). Supports: Q1 2026 revenue $41.1M down from $42.1M on supply-chain timing (https://www.placera.se/pressmeddelanden/tat-technologies-tat-technologies-reports-first-quarter-2026-results-backlog-and-long-term-agreements-increase-to-580-million-on-strong-demand-20260520). Cuts against: AAR's +31% repair growth (another finding).

findings.finding: The EPS bar ($0.38-0.43) sits above Q2's own adjusted EPS of $0.35 (adjusted net income $4.66M) on similar revenue. Q2 R&D rose 122.9% YoY and G&A 16.8%. Gross margin fell in OEM heat transfer (30.1% to 25.9%) and jet engine overhaul (51.9% to 32.0%), offset by MRO aviation components (16.5% to 23.0%). Meeting the EPS bar needs a margin step-up the Q2 cost trend does not show. Cap: the EPS basis is disputed (one aggregator lists Q1 'adjusted EPS 35c' while GAAP diluted EPS was $0.26).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS $0.35 vs $0.32 was a narrow beat next to the large revenue beat, and the stock gave back 6.4% the day after the print. Q3 2025 EPS $0.37 vs $0.40, a miss: -0.7% close to close after an after-hours pop.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregator EPS estimates are inconsistent ($0.38 vs $0.43 vs $0.48-0.50) and do not reconcile with the company's adjusted EPS of $0.35. The market may anchor on revenue and miss that the per-share bar requires margin expansion. If priced, EPS estimates would cluster near $0.35-0.38.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 6-K with the revenue finding, but on a different line (margin and opex, not revenue). Bar sources: https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/TATT, https://www.tickflow.io/stock/TATT/forecast.

findings.finding: Honeywell Aerospace's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-28) shows commercial aftermarket sales +2% organic, 'limited by mechanical component availability' from a small number of pacing suppliers. TAT's APU MRO (Honeywell 131-9 and 331 platforms) relies on Honeywell parts, and TAT's Q1 2026 shortfall was blamed on APU component supply disruption. Honeywell also cited 'encouraging signs from pacing suppliers'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 supply-chain shortfall (revenue down YoY) still produced +21% from a depressed price. The Q4 2025 print, when renewed supply disruption was flagged, fell 7.5% then 16.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a counterparty print that landed after TAT last spoke (08-05) and 5 days before TAT's print, on a 7-analyst microcap with no options market. If priced, TATT's consensus would have been trimmed after 10-28. B. Riley's target cut that day may be exactly that, filed separately.
findings.independence: Proxy: macro-to-company transmission that TAT has not confirmed for Q3. Stifel's April target cut was tied to APU component disruption (https://www.insidermonkey.com/blog/tatt-stock-gets-mixed-calls-but-the-real-story-may-be-ahead-1748188/). Net of the rest: APU is only part of the $27.7M MRO aviation segment, and the heat-transfer segments (about $23M) are unaffected.

findings.finding: AAR's fiscal Q1 2027 (June-August 2026, reported 2026-09-28) grew sales 24% to $918M, with Repair, Engineering & Software +31% and Parts Supply +31%, and guided next-quarter growth ex-legacy to 14-16%. This points to strong component MRO and parts demand overlapping two of TAT's three Q3 months.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: TAT's demand-driven revenue beat in Q2 2026 (+18% vs consensus) bought only +2.3% and then faded, so a demand read-through pays little.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer print after TAT's last report. TATT fell about 10% after it (from about $35.6 on 09-28 to $32), so the market did not carry the read-through into this name. If priced, TATT would not be making new lows into the print.
findings.independence: Proxy, an industry peer, not a TAT counterparty. The Honeywell finding points the other way on supply, not demand. Primary filing: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000001750/000110465926111403/tm2626100d2_ex99-1.htm

findings.finding: Short interest is 1.26M shares (2026-10-15 settlement): 9.7% of shares outstanding, roughly 20% of the float not held by 13G-filing Israeli institutions, and 9.4 days to cover. It was under 0.4M in May. The stock sits 1.5% above its 52-week low. The last print from a similar level ($32.69 into Q1 on 2026-05-20) squeezed +21%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: short interest about 0.40M (2026-05-15), stock at $32.69, small beat, +21.0%. Q2 2026: short interest 1.30M, stock $41.65, big beat, +2.3% then -6.4%. The squeeze only fired from the lows.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, not a fact about the quarter. The finding is the asymmetry: with 9.4 days to cover in a 116k-share daily tape, an in-line or better print forces buying the tape cannot easily supply. If the squeeze were priced, short interest would already have been covered (it fell only 16% from the September peak).
findings.independence: The 13G/A ownership data (e.g. Meitav 19.48%, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/808439/000117891326004913/primary_doc.xml) is the denominator for the float estimate. The unexplained drawdown itself is given zero weight.

findings.finding: B. Riley (Jeff Van Sinderen) cut its TATT price target from $65 to $60, keeping Buy, on 2026-10-28, five days before the print and the same day Honeywell reported. This suggests a preview estimate trim. That both lowers the bar and signals a softer quarter. The reason is not public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record for a pre-print target cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell 2-5% on 10-30 intraday ($33.50 to about $31.8-32.0), which may be partial pricing. If fully priced, consensus aggregators would show Q3 below $52.7M.
findings.independence: The same date as Honeywell's release suggests a common cause (the Honeywell finding), so this partly overlaps with it and is sized small. The ratings table is at https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tatt/ratings/.

findings.finding: Israeli institutional flows into the print are mixed. Meitav raised its stake to 19.48% (2,528,804 shares, event 2026-10-28), about 130k shares above the 2,398,855 at 2026-04-27. The More group cut from 5.42% (06-30) to 4.80% (09-30). Kranot filed a new 6.25% stake (event 2026-08-24).
findings.why_not_priced: Filed 2026-10-30, the day before the print weekend, on a name with no US media coverage of its 13G flows. A large holder adding near the lows is a modest supply absorber, not information about the quarter.

findings.finding: The shekel has stayed near 30-year highs through 2026 (about 2.8-3.0 per USD, vs about 3.35 in Q3 2025). TAT's Israeli operations (OEM heat transfer) have shekel costs. The Q4 2025 print flagged a >10% negative FX impact, and Q2 2026 OEM heat-transfer gross margin fell from 30.1% to 25.9% YoY. The YoY margin headwind persists in Q3; sequentially it is roughly flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4 2025 print, with FX and supply chain cited, fell 7.5% then 16.3% (one secondary source attributes it partly to the FX impact).
findings.source_date: 2026 (shekel at 30-year high; exact article date not confirmed from the URL)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is visible in Q2 margins and widely reported. Filed small for the YoY margin comparison in Q3.
findings.independence: Proxy. The margin effect is in the company's Q2 segment table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000808439/000117891326003835/exhibit_99-2.htm). A secondary source gives the Q4 FX attribution: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/tat-technologies-q4-earnings-call-highlights-2026-03-19/

findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call it aims to complete 'at least one acquisition this year', with due diligence done on several targets. It has a $75M revolver (signed 2026-06-04, $11.5M drawn at 06-30, accordion of up to $25M or 100% of EBITDA) and $54.6M cash. With two months left in 2026, a deal or a firm update could come with the Q3 call. The money buys acquisitions in a fragmented component-MRO market.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior TAT acquisition announced with a print in the window.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a stated intention, not an event. The sign depends on the price paid and how it is financed (no ATM/F-3 activity since the March F-3ASR). If a deal were expected, there would be no 9.4-days-to-cover short build.

findings.finding: Honeywell named TAT sole global authorized distributor of GTCP 331-200/250 APU spare parts (except Africa before 2030 and non-aftermarket OEMs) and extended its MRO licences to 2036. It was announced 2026-07-14, so Q3 is the first full quarter of distribution revenue. Products revenue was $15.3M in Q2. No revenue figure was given.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement day (2026-07-14) moved +4.56%. It has not yet appeared in a reported quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is unquantified, so consensus cannot have modelled it precisely. If priced, Q3 products revenue estimates would be broken out. They are not, and the stock is below its pre-announcement level ($32 vs about $39 then).
findings.independence: Honeywell's own page: https://www.honeywellaerospace.com/us/en/insights/articles/tat-technologies-named-sole-distributor-for-gtcp-331-200-250-apu-parts. Cuts against: Honeywell's own mechanical-parts constraint (another finding) may limit what TAT can distribute.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 operating cash flow was -$0.6M (vs +$6.9M in Q2 2025), driven by an $8.3M receivables build and a $3.5M inventory build. Inventory reached $85.2M against $75.5M at year-end. Q3 cash conversion is a quality-of-beat line: a reversal would support the print, a further build would undercut it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026's negative cash flow came with the +2.3% / -6.4% fade after a large beat.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is unknown, so it is sized at zero. Filed so a judge can weigh it.
findings.independence: Same 6-K as the EPS-bar finding, on a different line (cash flow). Finsee flags the same risk: https://finsee.ai/earnings/tatt/2026/q2/en/

rejected_candidates.detail: Five of the eight rows are non-earnings 6-Ks (06-03, 07-14 Honeywell deal, 07-27 proxy, 08-24 proxy amendment, 09-09 AGM results), and 08-05 appears three times (EDGAR filing list https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0000808439). Rebuilt from confirmed release dates and Yahoo closes (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TATT?range=2y&interval=1d): -0.7, -7.5 (then -16.3 next day), +21.0, +2.3, -12.4, about -5 to -7. Median absolute move about 7%.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The negatives (bar above the run-rate, Honeywell constraint, B. Riley trim) point the same way as the 20-day run-up of -9% and a rising short, so they are partly priced. The crowded short and the Q1 precedent from the same price level point the other way, so the evidence offsets.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): positioning cut from +1.5 to +0.8, keeping only the sourced short-interest and days-to-cover squeeze mechanism, not the 'stock is 48% off its high and below every target' argument.
Lesson 6 (bar): revenue bar has two roughly agreeing sources ($52.7M / $54.3M), so it is not capped. The EPS bar is disputed in basis, so that finding was capped from -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 7 and the core table (crowded short against a negative): revenue run-rate cut from -1.0 to -0.8 and the Honeywell proxy from -0.5 to -0.4 for the shrink, applied once.

Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): Honeywell parts constraint hits only the APU part of one segment (heat transfer is about $23M and unaffected), so it was cut from the -0.7 draft to -0.5 before the crowded-short trim.
Lesson 5 (proxies smaller): AAR read-through cut from +0.5 to +0.4.
Lesson 1 (beats sold here, misses punished): p_up moved from 50 to 48 and expected_move from 0.0 to -0.32. Findings were not re-shrunk for it.
FPI lesson: the base rate was rebuilt from confirmed releases (median about 7%), which sets abs_move_pct at 8 rather than the sealed 2.33. This was already done in the draft.
